SDE.charBuilder.tableSources.hint: Check the roll tables the builder draws from: Names & Trinkets (Ancestry step) and Backgrounds & Deities (the Origins step's Random). SDE.settings.levelGuidelines.intro: What a monster of each level is expected to look like. These numbers were derived from the monsters installed with the system, and every row is yours to edit — the guidelines are a starting point, not a rule.
SDE.settings.levelGuidelines.hpNote: HP is applied as ceil(level × 4.5) + CON, so the HP column below is the typical value for a creature with no Constitution modifier. Talent DC is advisory only and is never written to a monster.
SDE.settings.levelGuidelines.recalcHint: Rebuild the whole table from every NPC installed in this world.

SDE.settings.modesOfPlayMenu.name: Modes of Play
SDE.settings.modesOfPlayMenu.hint: The optional rules from the core rulebook (p.111), and Hard Luck from the Western Reaches (GMWR p.30). Every rule switches on by itself, so you can run one rule of a mode without the rest.
SDE.settings.modesOfPlayMenu.label: Modes of Play
SDE.settings.modesOfPlayMenu.grinderHint: Core rulebook p.111. Grinder takes effect in Shadowdark Extras' camping rest, so its switches are Extras' own settings.
SDE.settings.modesOfPlayMenu.grinderNeed: Grinder Mode changes how a rest heals, and the only rest in Foundry is Shadowdark Extras' camping rest. Install a version of Shadowdark Extras with Grinder Mode to switch it on here.
SDE.settings.modesOfPlayMenu.momentumHin: Core rulebook p.111. Exploding damage is the Shadowdark system's own setting, shown here.
SDE.settings.modesOfPlayMenu.momentumRep: Advantage on repeating an action that just failed is granted at the table; nothing here tracks it.
SDE.settings.modesOfPlayMenu.pulpHint: Core rulebook p.111. No maximum on luck tokens is the Shadowdark system's own setting, shown here.
SDE.settings.modesOfPlayMenu.pulpExtraAc: Spending a luck token for an extra action: spend it from the crawl strip's luck pill, which posts the spend to chat.
SDE.settings.modesOfPlayMenu.systemMissi: This rule is a setting of the Shadowdark system, and the installed version of the system doesn't have it.
SDE.settings.modesOfPlayMenu.hardLuckHin: Game Master's Guide to the Western Reaches p.30.
SDE.settings.modeBlitzLights.name: Light sources last 30 minutes
SDE.settings.modeBlitzLights.hint: A torch, a lantern or a light spell lasts 30 minutes instead of an hour.
SDE.settings.modeChaosInitiative.name: Reroll initiative every round
SDE.settings.modeChaosInitiative.hint: At the start of every round after the first, everyone rolls initiative again and the turn order is rebuilt.
SDE.settings.modeDeadlyTimer.name: Death timers are always 1
SDE.settings.modeDeadlyTimer.hint: A dying character has 1 round to live, whatever their Constitution.
SDE.settings.modeDeadlyStabilize.name: Stabilizing is DC 18
SDE.settings.modeDeadlyStabilize.hint: Stabilizing a dying character is an Intelligence check at DC 18 instead of DC 15.
SDE.settings.modeFatality.name: Characters die at 0 HP
SDE.settings.modeFatality.hint: There is no dying: a character reduced to 0 HP is dead.
SDE.settings.modeHunterXp.name: XP for defeated monsters
SDE.settings.modeHunterXp.hint: When a combat ends, every character in it gets XP for each defeated monster: half its level, rounded down, and 1 for a level 1 monster.
SDE.settings.modePulpSessionLuck.name: 1d4 luck at the start of each session
SDE.settings.modePulpSessionLuck.hint: Starting a session sets each party member's luck tokens to 1d4.
SDE.settings.modePulpLuckCrit.name: Spend luck to turn a hit into a critical hit
SDE.settings.modePulpLuckCrit.hint: After an attack hits, its owner can spend a luck token to make it a critical hit.
SDE.settings.modePulpForceReroll.name: Spend luck to make the GM reroll
SDE.settings.modePulpForceReroll.hint: A player can spend a luck token to make the GM reroll a roll the player can see.
SDE.settings.modeHardLuckEffects.name: No luck rerolls with luck-granting effects
SDE.settings.modeHardLuckEffects.hint: Luck can't reroll a roll made under an effect that grants luck itself, such as Bless, Trance or a Seer's Omen.

SDE.settings.scavengerWatchAmmo.hint: Firing your last arrow or bolt also triggers Scavenger.

SDE.hexMap.tip.read: Read every hex of this scene's image in your browser, so the Legend and Classify have a picture of each one. Nothing is uploaded, and no terrain is decided.
SDE.hexMap.tip.legend: Sort every hex picture into groups of look-alikes and show one card per group. Reads the map first if it needs to.
SDE.hexMap.tip.classify: Tag every hex you have NOT tagged yourself by whichever of your own hand-tagged hexes it looks most like. Reads the map first if it needs to. Unsure hexes go to the Review queue.
SDE.hexMap.tip.show: Which hexes the grid below shows you
SDE.hexMap.tip.hexKey: The journal entry of book text for this map's keyed hexes
SDE.hexMap.tip.pinKeyed: One map note per keyed hex of the chosen book text on this scene, each opening its journal page
SDE.hexMap.tip.showTags: Draw every tag on the map itself: a colour per terrain, dots for river, path and coast, an amber ring on the unsure automatic cells. Click a hex there to change it. Press again to hide.
SDE.hexMap.tip.showRegions: Colour every hex by the region the map's own borders put it in. One colour per region.
SDE.hexMap.tip.showZones: Show whether a wandering check on each hex would find a table: green rolls, amber needs a time of day or a compass half the map cannot say, grey has no table for that region.
SDE.hexMap.zone.unnamed: enclosure {id} — import the book's key locations to name it
SDE.hexMap.zone.inferred: {region} — guessed from the nearest keyed hex, not read off the print
SDE.hexMap.label.wholeEnclosure: Apply to the whole enclosure ({n} hexes)
SDE.hexMap.notify.regionCleared: {n} hexes back to what the map says.
SDE.hexMap.tip.brush: Pick a terrain once, then click or drag across the hexes that have it wrong. A whole stroke is one change, and Undo puts it back.
SDE.hexMap.tip.more: Map size, read the image again, import, export, build a painted map, reference tile, clear
SDE.hexMap.tip.readAgain: Read the pictures from the scene image again; every tag is kept
SDE.hexMap.tip.learnFrom: Bring in every hex you tagged by hand on another go at this same print, as examples for Classify. Your tags here are left alone.
SDE.hexMap.btn.learnFrom: Start from a map you have done
SDE.hexMap.tip.import: Import tags from a CSV (hex_id, tags) or a JSON exported here
SDE.hexMap.tip.export: Download this scene's tags as JSON
SDE.hexMap.tip.art: Load your own manifest of which tile paints each hex
SDE.hexMap.tip.reference: Put this map image on another hex scene as a hidden, locked tile for tracing rivers and roads
SDE.hexMap.tip.sendExtras: Put the hex details on this map in Shadowdark Extras: terrain, regions, names and descriptions. Nothing is painted over the print.
SDE.hexMap.tip.buildPainted: Build a new Shadowdark Extras scene painted from these tags, instead of putting the details on this map
SDE.hexMap.tip.clear: Remove every tag and the anchor from this scene

SDE.hexMap.tip.sensitivity: Higher values lower the overlay thresholds: raise it if paths and rivers are missed, lower it if plain cells pick up overlays.
SDE.hexMap.legend.howTo: Name what the pictures have in common. A mountain with a river across it is still mountain — rivers and roads are found separately. Use village, town, city, city state or keyed location for the marker symbols.

SDE.hexMap.legend.opened: {size} cells — answer these {picks} one by one; the rest go to the classifier
SDE.hexMap.tip.coast: Saved on this scene; not included in dataset networks yet.
SDE.hexMap.sheet.leaveAlone: Leaving a hex alone says the classifier got it right.
SDE.hexMap.tip.confirm: Accepts every hex on this sheet as it now reads — the ones you changed and the ones you left — and takes them out of the review queue.
SDE.hexMap.tip.others: A different {n} hexes. Nothing on this sheet is confirmed or changed.
SDE.hexMap.dev.openFirst: Open the Hex Tagger and read the map first.
SDE.hexMap.dev.tagFirst: Tag some hexes by hand first: they are the only ground truth there is.
SDE.hexMap.dev.disabled: Hex map developer tools are disabled.
SDE.hexMap.dev.verifiedFirst: Open the Hex Tagger on a verified map first.
SDE.hexMap.dev.needVerified: This needs a map you have verified by hand: at least 200 hexes tagged yourself.
SDE.hexMap.notify.gmOnly: Only a GM can tag hex maps.

SDE.hexMap.notify.noOtherScene: No other scene has hexes you tagged by hand.

SDE.hexMap.notify.artForgotten: Tile art forgotten; hexes will be painted from their terrain.

SDE.hexMap.notify.learnNothing: Nothing to bring over from "{from}": every hex it has, you have already tagged here.

SDE.hexMap.notify.classified: Tagged {auto} hexes from your {examples} hand-tagged examples; {fixes} then corrected by their neighbours; {coasts} marked as coast for touching water; {review} went to the Review queue.
SDE.hexMap.notify.dropped: {n} cells are no longer on the map; their tags were dropped.
SDE.hexMap.notify.datasetInvalid: Hex dataset failed its contract check: {error}
SDE.hexMap.notify.sent: Sent "{name}" to Shadowdark Extras ({hexes} keyed hexes, {cells} tagged cells{art}).
SDE.hexMap.notify.onPrintFirst: This map is now a Shadowdark Extras hexcrawl: {hexes} hexes sent with their terrain, regions and descriptions. Nothing was painted over the print.
SDE.hexMap.notify.onPrint: Updated {hexes} hexes on this map in Shadowdark Extras.
SDE.hexMap.notify.needsAdopt: This version of Shadowdark Extras can't put hex details on a map you already have. Update it, or use Build painted map under More.
SDE.hexMap.notify.adoptFailed: Shadowdark Extras wouldn't take this map: {error}
SDE.hexMap.notify.notTopLeft: Shadowdark Extras numbers a map from the scene's top-left cell, and this map's hex {first} isn't there, so the details would land on the wrong hexes. Use Build painted map under More instead.
SDE.hexMap.notify.importEmpty: Nothing to import from {file}: no hex_id/tags columns, tag flag or dataset found.
SDE.hexMap.notify.artEmpty: Nothing usable in {file}: no rows with a hex number and a tile.
SDE.hexMap.notify.artLoaded: {kept} of {total} rows kept{skipped}, {icons} with a centre icon.
SDE.hexMap.notify.artSkipped: ({n} are not hexes on this map)
SDE.hexMap.notify.parityMismatch: "{name}" lowers its {lowered} columns but the map lowers its {shifted} ones; set its grid to Hexagonal Columns ({shifted}) so the hexes line up.
SDE.hexMap.notify.referencePlaced: Reference tile placed on "{name}", hidden and locked. Delete it when tracing is done: hidden tiles still reach player clients with the image's URL.
SDE.hexMap.app.title: Hex Tagger
SDE.hexMap.learn.title: Start from a map you have already done
SDE.hexMap.learn.hint: Every hex you tagged yourself there is copied here as a hand tag, and becomes an example for Classify. Hexes you have already tagged here are left alone. Hexes are matched by their printed number, so this is for another go at the same print — on a different map the numbers mean something else.
SDE.hexMap.suspect.title: A card may be named wrong
SDE.hexMap.suspect.lead: These cards do not look like the other cards you gave the same name to — each one looks more like a card you named something else:
SDE.hexMap.suspect.row: the card of {size} hexes you called {name} looks {times}× more like {looksLike}
SDE.hexMap.suspect.why: Naming a card is one answer for every hex in it, so one wrong name is hundreds of wrong hexes. Go back and look at its pictures, or apply anyway if you are sure.
SDE.hexMap.unnamed.title: Cards left unnamed
SDE.hexMap.unnamed.one: {cards} card is unnamed, covering {hexes} hexes (the largest is {largest}).
SDE.hexMap.unnamed.many: {cards} cards are unnamed, covering {hexes} hexes (the largest is {largest}).
SDE.hexMap.unnamed.why: Unnamed hexes are not left alone: they are guessed from the cards you did name, so a card that is its own thing — a river with no terrain under it, a band of ice — comes back as whatever looks nearest. Name it, or say it is a keyed location, unless you mean the classifier to guess.
SDE.hexMap.import.title: Import hex tags
SDE.hexMap.import.hint: A CSV with hex_id and tags columns (semicolon-separated, source optional), or a JSON exported by this tagger or a hexcrawl dataset. Imported rows replace the cell's tags.
SDE.hexMap.art.title: Tile art for this map
SDE.hexMap.art.hint: A JSON manifest saying which tile each hex is painted with: hex number to base_hex, and overlay_asset for a centre icon. Paths are relative to Shadowdark Extras' assets/.
SDE.hexMap.art.skipped: Rows whose id is not a hex number on this map are skipped.
SDE.hexMap.clear.title: Clear hex tags
SDE.hexMap.clear.confirm: Remove every tag and the anchor from {scene}? The map image and grid are untouched.
SDE.hexMap.reference.hint: Place this scene's map image on another scene as a hidden, locked, half-transparent tile, scaled so its hex field covers that scene's first {cols} × {rows} cells.
SDE.hexMap.reference.asMap: Use the print as the map, not as a tracing aid
SDE.hexMap.tip.asMap: Places the print visible and opaque over the painted hexes, so the table plays on the publisher's own map while the scene keeps everything Shadowdark Extras needs — its grid, its hex records and its explorer. Hide the tile later to go back to the painted map.
SDE.hexMap.label.notAllSame: these are not all the same
SDE.hexMap.error.noCells: No grid cells overlap the background image.
SDE.hexMap.error.tainted: The background image is not same-origin, so its pixels cannot be read. Put the file in your Foundry data directory.
SDE.hexMap.flow.pickHint: Pick the map image. It is read in your browser; the hex grid is found on its own, and the image is then copied into this world's folder as the scene background.
SDE.hexMap.flow.cornersMissedOne: No printed hex outline where the grid puts its {corners} corner. Compare the crops below; correct the counts if a row or column is off by one, or cancel and set the scene up by hand.
SDE.hexMap.flow.cornersMissedMany: No printed hex outline where the grid puts its {corners} corners. Compare the crops below; correct the counts if a row or column is off by one, or cancel and set the scene up by hand.
SDE.hexMap.flow.cornersOk: Checked: the grid lands on a printed hex at all four corners. Nothing to do here but Create scene; the crops below are the proof.
SDE.hexMap.flow.checkCrops: Check the four crops. The blue hex should sit on a printed one.
SDE.hexMap.flow.found: {cols} × {rows} flat-top hexes, {px} × {py} px, {lowered} columns half a hex lower
SDE.hexMap.flow.onlyThree: The three boxes below are all you can change. Where the grid sits and how big it is were measured off the print — if the blue is not on a hex at all, cancel rather than fiddle. Pointy-top maps are not supported.
SDE.hexMap.flow.openPrint: Open the print on its own, with no marks on it
SDE.hexMap.flow.marks: Every blue mark is a hex the detector found: an outline on the corner hexes, and a dot at the centre of every fortieth cell across the overview, which is why most hexes there carry no dot. Nothing on this screen marks a fault. Drag the window edge to enlarge; clicking the overview opens your print on its own, with no marks on it.
SDE.hexMap.flow.firstNumHint: The printed number of the top-left cell; every other cell is numbered from it.
SDE.hexMap.notify.badCounts: Columns and rows must be positive and the first number 3 or 4 digits.
SDE.hexMap.notify.gmOnlySetup: Only a GM can set up hex maps.
SDE.hexMap.notify.noGrid: No hex grid found on this image. Hand-drawn or faint grids can be tagged the old way: make a scene, align it, and open the Hex tagger.
SDE.hexMap.notify.notAnImage: Could not read {file} as an image: {error}
SDE.hexMap.notify.readingImage: Reading {file} ({w} × {h})… this takes a few seconds.
SDE.hexMap.notify.sceneCreated: Scene "{name}" created: {cols} × {rows} hexes on a {size} px grid. Opening the tagger on its legend.
SDE.hexMap.brush.title: Hex Brush
SDE.hexMap.brush.hintPicked: Click or drag hexes to make them {tags}.
SDE.hexMap.brush.hintNone: Pick a terrain, then click or drag hexes on the map.
SDE.hexMap.brush.nothingToUndo: No stroke to undo: Undo puts back the last one, and only the last one.
SDE.hexMap.notify.gmOnlyReview: Only a GM can review hex tags.
SDE.hexMap.notify.noNumbering: This scene has no hex numbering yet: set it up with Hex map from image, or sample it in the tagger and set the anchor.
SDE.hexMap.notify.overlayShown: Hex tags shown on the map. Click a hex to change its tags; the button hides them again.
SDE.hexMap.edit.title: Hex {num}
SDE.hexMap.notify.gmOnlyPin: Only a GM can pin keyed hexes.
SDE.hexMap.error.notHex: The active scene does not use a hexagonal grid.
SDE.hexMap.error.pointyTop: Only flat-top column hex grids are supported in this version; this scene uses pointy-top rows.
SDE.hexMap.error.noBackground: The active scene has no background image, or it has not finished loading.
SDE.importer.type.diceTip: How many dice and their size, e.g. 3d6 = 3 columns each rolled on a d6 (6 rows). Fixes the grid shape even for a messy or header-less paste. Leave blank to auto-detect.
SDE.importer.seed.openPdfTip: Open the source PDF at the cited page to copy from
SDE.importer.seed.grabTextTip: Pull the cited page's text straight into the paste box (no drag-selecting). Uses Foundry's built-in PDF engine; two-column pages come out in reading order.
SDE.importer.seed.grabFromPdfTip: This entry has no cited page — pull it from the book by page. Opens the page-range extractor with the book pre-selected.
SDE.importer.seed.thenParse: — paste that section and click Parse.
SDE.importer.seed.parsedOk: Parsed "{name}": {rows} rows on {formula} — correct. Review below, then Create tables.
SDE.importer.seed.parsedProblem: {problem}. Check the paste for those lines; the rows are flagged on the card below.
SDE.importer.seed.parsedExpected: it should be {expected} — check the paste for missing lines.
SDE.importer.paste.label: Paste a raw dump from your Shadowdark book — monsters, items, spells, tables, or a mix:
SDE.importer.source.label: Source
SDE.importer.tools.sourcePdfsTip: Upload your own PDFs of the Shadowdark books. Each is linked to a source so the Open-PDF buttons jump to the cited page. Files stay in your world.
SDE.importer.tools.extractSub: Pull a page's text into the box
SDE.importer.tools.extractTip: Pull clean, reading-ordered text out of one of your uploaded books (any page or range) straight into the paste box.
SDE.importer.tools.exportSub: Back up the whole suite to a file
SDE.importer.tools.exportTip: Download all imported content (every Shadowdark Enhancer compendium pack) as one JSON bundle.
SDE.importer.tools.importBundleSub: Restore a suite from a file
SDE.importer.tools.importBundleTip: Import a bundle file into this world's compendium packs. Existing documents are never overwritten.
SDE.importer.tools.hexMapSub: Upload a map, get an aligned scene
SDE.importer.tools.hexMapTip: Pick a hex-map image: the grid is found on its own, the scene is created aligned, and the tagger opens ready.
SDE.importer.tools.hexTaggerTip: Tag the terrain of every hex on the active hex-map scene from a contact sheet, then hand the dataset to Shadowdark Extras or download it. Reads your own map image in the browser; nothing ships with the module.
SDE.importer.tools.keyLocationsSub: A book's whole hex key, region by region
SDE.importer.tools.keyLocationsTip: Read every keyed location of a book out of your own PDF and file it as journal pages: one entry per region, one page per hex, with the region's summary table alongside. Safe to run again — pages you already have are updated, not duplicated.
SDE.importer.note.offline: Parsing is offline — nothing is uploaded. Auto-detect sorts a mixed dump; pick a specific type to force it (the box shows an example of that type's format). Fields the parser wasn't sure about are highlighted.
SDE.importer.downtime.title: Downtime
SDE.importer.downtime.pasteFrom: Paste the downtime pages from your own copy of {book}
SDE.importer.downtime.thenParse: , then Parse. The outcome text is stored in this world only. Switching books clears the parse — pick the book first.
SDE.importer.monsters.title: Monsters ({n})
SDE.importer.common.name: name
SDE.importer.items.title: Items ({n})
SDE.importer.items.statLineTip: Parsed weapon/armor stats — fine-tune on the item sheet after import
SDE.importer.spells.title: Spells ({n})
SDE.importer.cls.spellListTip: Which spell list this class casts from — pick an existing caster (a knightly order might cast from the witch list) or keep its own new list
SDE.importer.cls.weaponsTip: Named weapons; combine with the All checkboxes for grants like “All melee weapons, crossbow”
SDE.importer.cls.armorTip: Named armor; combines with the All armor checkbox
SDE.importer.cls.stage1: Stage 1 imports the class body only. The talent table, titles, and spells known are imported next in Class · Roll Tables and attached to this class.
SDE.importer.cls.noTable: No table parsed from the paste — add rows below to build one (2d6 by default).
SDE.importer.cls.mergeTip: Drop the options — this row becomes one talent named by its effect text
SDE.importer.cls.grand: links every option above + Distribute to Stats
SDE.importer.cls.splitTip: This row is a pick — split the text into options
SDE.importer.cls.spellsKnownTip: Spells known per level (tier 1 · 2 · 3 · …) — parsed from the SPELLS KNOWN table; commits to the class sheet's grid
SDE.importer.sup.attachAria: Class to attach these tables to
SDE.importer.sup.titlesHint: Paste a TITLES block above to fill these, or add bands by hand (Levels / Lawful / Chaotic / Neutral).
SDE.importer.boats.title: Boats ({n})
SDE.importer.hex.pinTip: One map note per keyed hex on the scene you are viewing, each opening its page
SDE.importer.hex.pinNote: Pin puts the keyed locations on your map scene as notes that open their pages (the crawl's journal is copied into the world for that).
SDE.importer.hex.noSceneNote: To put the keyed locations on a map, view the scene made by Hex map from image and come back here.
SDE.importer.hex.extrasNote: Send to Extras builds a painted hex crawl scene in Shadowdark Extras from the filed pages and keyed rows instead.
SDE.importer.hex.downloadNote: Download dataset saves this crawl as JSON (keyed hexes, terrain, networks) for Shadowdark Extras or another world; it is built from your own book text.
SDE.importer.hex.title: Hex key ({n})
SDE.importer.hex.titlePlaceholder: Journal entry name, e.g. the region or map title
SDE.importer.hex.filedUnder: One journal page per hex, filed under
SDE.importer.hex.filedRest: in the Journals pack. References to other hexes in this paste become links; re-pasting the same crawl updates its pages.
SDE.importer.hex.summaryRows: {n} keyed summary rows (number, region, terrain, name) will be filed on the entry for the Extras hand-off.
SDE.importer.hex.book.title: Key locations from a book
SDE.importer.hex.book.lead: Read a book's keyed locations out of your own PDF and file them as journal pages.
SDE.importer.hex.book.notes: One journal entry per region, one page per keyed hex, with the region's summary table filed on the entry. Nothing is uploaded and no book text ships with the module. Running this again updates the pages you already have rather than duplicating them.
SDE.importer.hex.book.noBooks: No book has a verified key-location page map yet.
SDE.importer.hex.book.gmOnly: Only a GM can import key locations.
SDE.importer.hex.book.gutter: Text crossed the column gutter on {pages} pages, most often {what} — usually a footnote that spans both columns. The locations still imported; compare those pages against the book if one reads wrong: p{list}.
SDE.importer.hex.book.working: Reading key locations from the PDF…
SDE.importer.hex.book.done: Filed {hexes} keyed hexes across {regions} regions from {book}.
SDE.importer.hex.book.failed: {n} region(s) could not be read; the first was {first}. See the console for details.
SDE.importer.tables.title: Tables ({n})
SDE.importer.tables.replacementTip: On: results can repeat. Off: each result is removed after drawn.
SDE.importer.tables.folderTip: Folder this table is filed under.
SDE.importer.tables.folderAria: Folder this table is filed under
SDE.importer.tables.bestEffort: Best-effort column split — check the cells.
SDE.importer.tables.linkTip: Draws as a link to this compendium item
SDE.importer.gen.title: Generators ({n})
SDE.importer.gen.cartesianNote: Every column combination is spelled out into one long, fully-visible table — {total} rows in total, rolled with a single die. The grid below is what you're combining, not what gets created; each generator's own row count is shown beside its name. Nothing is hidden, so you can read and edit every result afterwards.
SDE.importer.gen.note: A generator rolls every column once and joins the cells in order. Each grid row is a die face; each column is rolled independently. Fix any flagged cells below, then Create — roll it from the table sheet or Roll Tables directory.
SDE.importer.gen.dieTip: Die each column is rolled on.
SDE.importer.gen.joinTip: Text placed between column results when combined.
SDE.importer.gen.expands: Expands to {rows} rows ({math}), rolled as {formula} — one row per combination.
SDE.importer.skipped.title: Skipped ({n})
SDE.importer.manage.title: Manage
SDE.importer.manage.legendMissing: missing = importable. Import seeds the paste box (paste from your own book).
SDE.importer.manage.lockedTip: Only what you haven't imported yet
SDE.importer.manage.importedTip: Only what's already in your library
SDE.importer.manage.searchTip: Filter the tree by name, book or page — matching folders open on their own
SDE.importer.manage.batchTip: Run every unlock in this list for you — grab, parse and create, reading from your own uploaded books. Nothing already imported is touched.
SDE.importer.manage.noPdf: Link your books under Tools → Source PDFs to import them automatically.
SDE.importer.manage.noPdfTip: Rows whose book has no linked PDF, or no page citation, can only be imported by hand.
SDE.importer.manage.stopTip: Stop after the current entry finishes
SDE.importer.manage.noMatchClear: — clear the search to see the whole library.
SDE.importer.manage.allImported: Nothing left to unlock — everything in this list is imported.
SDE.importer.manage.noneImported: Nothing imported yet — switch to Still locked to see what's available.
SDE.importer.manage.newTip: Only what this module update added and you haven't imported yet
SDE.importer.manage.allNewImported: Nothing new left — you've imported everything this update added.
SDE.importer.news.title: Shadowdark Enhancer — new content
SDE.importer.news.body: This update added content you can import into this world ({n}). Open the Importer Hub to see what's new?
SDE.importer.manage.loading: Expand to load the census & cleanup tools…
SDE.importer.tree.presentTip: Present in this world / the suite
SDE.importer.tree.lockedTip: Not yet imported — paste from your own book to import
SDE.importer.tree.newTip: Added by a module update since this world last looked
SDE.importer.tree.batchNodeTip: Import everything still locked in “{label}” — grabs, parses and creates each entry from your own uploaded books
SDE.importer.tree.fillAllTip: Read each imported patron's page from your linked source PDF and fill in every Patron Item in “{label}” that has no description yet
SDE.importer.tree.fillOneTip: Read this patron's page from your linked source PDF and fill in the Patron Item's description
SDE.importer.tree.importTip: Import “{name}” — opens the importer (paste from your own book)
SDE.importer.bundle.exportFailed: Bundle export failed — see the console for details.
SDE.importer.bundle.title: Import Bundle
SDE.importer.bundle.badJson: That file is not valid JSON.
SDE.importer.bundle.skipNote: Documents already in your packs (same id) are skipped — nothing is overwritten or deleted.
SDE.importer.bundle.importFailed: Bundle import failed — see the console for details.
SDE.importer.notify.gmOnlyPdfs: Only a GM can manage source PDFs.
SDE.importer.batch.alreadyRunning: A batch import is already running.
SDE.importer.batch.noneRunnableOne: Nothing can run unattended here — {n} row needs a source PDF or a hand paste.
SDE.importer.batch.noneRunnableMany: Nothing can run unattended here — {n} rows need a source PDF or a hand paste.
SDE.importer.batch.nothingLeft: Nothing left to import here — every row is already in your library.
SDE.importer.batch.confirmLeadOne: Import {jobs} entry from {scope}, covering {covered} of the {locked} rows still locked:
SDE.importer.batch.confirmLeadMany: Import {jobs} entries from {scope}, covering {covered} of the {locked} rows still locked:
SDE.importer.batch.blockedOne: {n} row can't run unattended (no linked PDF, no page cite, or a hand-paste entry). It is listed in the report at the end.
SDE.importer.batch.blockedMany: {n} rows can't run unattended (no linked PDF, no page cite, or a hand-paste entry). They're listed in the report at the end.
SDE.importer.batch.confirmNote: Each entry runs the same unlock → grab → parse → create you'd click by hand, reading from your own uploaded books. Anything already in your library is kept as it is — nothing is replaced or deleted — and anything that fails a quality check is left for you to review. You can stop the run at any point.
SDE.importer.batch.noBookLinked: no linked PDF for {books} — upload one under Source PDFs, then run this again
SDE.importer.report.title: Batch import report
SDE.importer.notify.notFound: Couldn't find “{name}” — it may have been renamed or deleted since the census ran.
SDE.importer.notify.gmOnlyCull: Only a GM can cull duplicates.
SDE.importer.cull.noGroupMonsters: Duplicate group not found — refresh the Monsters tab.
SDE.importer.cull.noGroupItems: Duplicate group not found — refresh the Items tab.
SDE.importer.cull.nothingToCull: Nothing to cull — only one member selected as keeper.
SDE.importer.cull.actorsNote: Only pack copies in sde-actors are deleted. World actors and _Backup docs are never touched.
SDE.importer.pdf.writeupFailed: Couldn't pull the “{name}” writeup from the source PDF — paste it by hand, or see the console.
SDE.importer.pdf.tablesFailed: Couldn't pull the {type} tables from the source PDF — paste them by hand, or see the console.
SDE.importer.pdf.noneLinkedEntry: No source PDF is linked for this entry, or it has no page cite. Use “Source PDFs” to upload the book.

SDE.importer.pdf.pulledModes: Pulled page {page} in {modes} column modes — the box holds it once per mode. Review, then Parse.
SDE.importer.pdf.pulledPages: Pulled {n} pages into the paste box — review, then Parse.
SDE.importer.pdf.pulledPage: Pulled page {page} into the paste box — review, then Parse.
SDE.importer.pdf.noneLinked: No source PDFs are linked yet. Use “Source PDFs” to upload your books first.
SDE.importer.pdf.bookNotLinked: That book isn't linked to a PDF.
SDE.importer.pdf.needPage: Enter at least one valid page number.
SDE.importer.pdf.readFailed: Couldn't read text from that PDF — {error} (details in the console).
SDE.importer.pdf.pagesNoText: Those pages have no selectable text (likely scanned or art pages).
SDE.importer.pdf.extracted: Extracted {n} page(s) into the paste box{note} — review, then Parse.
SDE.importer.cull.itemsNote: Only pack copies in sde-items are deleted. World items and _Backup docs are never touched.
SDE.importer.extract.title: Extract text from PDF
SDE.importer.extract.lead: Pull clean, reading-ordered text out of one of your uploaded books using Foundry's built-in PDF engine — nothing is uploaded.
SDE.importer.extract.notes: These are the book's own PDF page numbers (including cover/credits), not the printed page. Auto-detect handles two-column spell/table pages; force Single/Two if a page comes out jumbled. A wide equipment table (Item · Cost · Quantity · Slot) reads best as Single column — Auto-detect scrambles its columns into a jumble.
SDE.importer.parse.needTableCompound: Paste a table first, then click Compound.
SDE.importer.parse.needTableCartesian: Paste a table first, then click Cartesian.
SDE.importer.parse.needDowntime: Paste the {book} downtime pages (pg {pages}) first, then click Parse.
SDE.importer.parse.downtimeFailed: Couldn't parse that downtime page — see the console.
SDE.importer.parse.downtimeNoMatch: Nothing matched — paste the {book} downtime pages ({pages}), headers and DC lines included.

SDE.importer.parse.noBoats: No boats found — paste the book's BOATS table (Name/Cost/Speed/AC/HP/Gear Slots/Properties).

SDE.importer.parse.mountsMissingMany: {n} requested mounts weren't found among the statblocks on the pasted pages: {names}.
SDE.importer.parse.tablesMissing: {n} of {total} tables in this unlock weren't found — see Skipped.
SDE.importer.parse.shapeEmpty: Shape parse produced nothing — check the pasted section.
SDE.importer.parse.shapeMismatch: “{name}” has a known layout that the pasted text doesn't match. Use “Grab text” to pull the page from the linked PDF, or paste the rows with their column spacing intact — anything below is a best-effort guess.
SDE.importer.parse.noCompound: No compound generator recognized — need a die header (e.g. d6) and 2+ column labels (e.g. Detail 1, Detail 2…).
SDE.importer.parse.cartesianTooBig: "{name}" would be {rows} rows (over {cap}) — use the Compound button for that one.

SDE.importer.srcpdf.title: Source PDFs
SDE.importer.srcpdf.lead: Upload your own PDFs of the Shadowdark books. Each is linked to a source so the importer's Open PDF buttons jump straight to the cited page. Files go to assets/ on this server, where every world finds them — nothing leaves your machine. If your host refuses a book-sized upload, copy the PDF into your Foundry data folder yourself and use Link a file on the server instead.
SDE.importer.srcpdf.tip: Double-click a linked book to open it in Foundry's PDF viewer.
SDE.importer.srcpdf.linkExisting: Link a file on the server
SDE.importer.srcpdf.notFound: That book's PDF couldn't be found.
SDE.importer.srcpdf.notPdf: That doesn't look like a PDF file.
SDE.importer.srcpdf.needName: Give the book a name before uploading it.
SDE.importer.srcpdf.uploadFailed: The server refused that upload. A book-sized PDF is usually blocked by the web server or proxy in front of Foundry, not by Foundry itself — copy the file into your Foundry data folder yourself, then use “Link a file on the server”.

SDE.importer.app.title: Importer
SDE.importer.compound.title: Compound Generator
SDE.importer.compound.lead: Roll every column once and combine the results in order (result 1 + result 2 + … = final).
SDE.importer.compound.notes: 3d6 = 3 columns, each rolled on a d6 (6 rows). Leave blank to auto-detect from the paste.
SDE.importer.cartesian.title: Cartesian Table
SDE.importer.cartesian.lead: Spell out every combination of the columns into one long, fully-visible table (no hidden roll-each-column logic).
SDE.importer.cartesian.notes: 3d6 = 3 columns each with 6 rows → a 216-row table. Insert | between columns in your paste to set the splits yourself. Over 25,000 rows is blocked — use Compound for those.

SDE.hexMap.note.needsOrigin: Type the printed number of any hex below, then Set. The rest are numbered from it.
